## 'Not at war anywhere in the world' claim (July 2024)

In a live address on the evening of Wednesday, 24 July 2024, delivered days after he announced his withdrawal from the presidential race and endorsed Vice President [[kamala-harris|Kamala Harris]], Biden claimed that the United States is "not at war anywhere in the world."[{N}] He said serving as president had been the "honor" of his life and that he had decided to "pass the torch to a new generation," adding: "I need to unite my party… nothing can come in the way of saving our democracy, and that includes personal ambition."[{N}] He also pledged to "keep working to ensure America remains strong, and secure, and the leader of the free world," describing himself as the first president this century to report that the country was not at war anywhere.[{N}]

Badlands commentator [[ashe-in-america|Ashe in America]] rejected the claim, arguing that the Obama–Biden administration's hallmark was the redefinition of metrics and common meanings and that the definition of 'war' was now being changed.[{N}] The commentary cited Ukraine and Gaza as evidence to the contrary, including $320 million spent on the Gaza pier structure that eventually sank, along with US funding of Taiwan's stand against China and conflict in Sudan, and the National Security Supplemental pushed by Jake Sullivan and John Kirby and eventually passed.[{N}] The argument concluded that the scale and duration of hot conflicts worldwide would be impossible without US funding, making the United States not merely 'at war' but the propagator of multiple wars under Biden.[{N}]

During the same period, Biden was scheduled to meet Israeli prime minister [[benjamin-netanyahu|Benjamin Netanyahu]] in the Oval Office before Netanyahu travelled to Florida to meet [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]].[{N}]
entities/benjamin-netanyahu.md:
## July 2024 Washington visit and Trump meeting

In late July 2024 Netanyahu travelled to the United States, addressing a joint session of Congress, meeting President [[joe-biden|Joe Biden]] in the Oval Office and holding a private meeting with Vice President [[kamala-harris|Kamala Harris]], before flying to Florida to meet [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]] on the Friday.[{N}] Ahead of that meeting Trump told Fox News that Israel must end its war with [[hamas|Hamas]] quickly and bring the remaining hostages home, saying Israel was "getting decimated with this publicity" and "is not very good at public relations."[{N}] Trump had earlier blamed Netanyahu for allowing the 7 October attacks to occur, saying intelligence warnings were well known in advance.[{N}]

Badlands commentary by [[ghostofbasedpatrickhenry|GhostofBasedPatrickHenry]] read Trump's remarks as the completion of a public "turn" against Netanyahu, and interpreted the "public relations" line as a reference to growing antisemitic sentiment as global opinion soured on Israel's conduct of the war.[{N}] The commentary argued that a secular government conflating itself with a world religion causes practitioners of that religion worldwide to absorb contempt directed at the Israeli state.[{N}]

The Hostages and Missing Families Forum said that "the information provided to the hostages' families did not accurately reflect the situation's reality," calling the delays "a deliberate sabotage of the chance to bring our loved ones back" that "effectively undermines the negotiations and indicates a serious moral failure."[{N}] Badlands commentary contended that Netanyahu would do whatever he could to subvert a ceasefire deal, because the return of all hostages would strip him of the moral imperative for war and lead radicals in his cabinet to collapse his government if peace broke out; it further raised the possibility that Netanyahu or cabinet members could have helped facilitate the October 7th attack.[{N}]
entities/volodymyr-zelensky.md:
## Peace-talk pressure and domestic warnings (July 2024)

After [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]] and Zelensky held a phone call that both sides characterised positively, Trump said that as "your next President of the United States, I will bring peace to the world and end the war that has cost so many lives and devastated countless innocent families," adding that "both sides will be able to come together and negotiate a deal that ends the violence and paves a path forward to prosperity."[{N}] Influential Ukrainian officials responded by warning Zelensky against moving too hastily to the negotiating table; he had previously refused to sit down with Moscow so long as [[vladimir-putin|Vladimir Putin]] led Russia.[{N}] Devastating troop losses, a shortage of artillery ammunition relative to better-armed Russian forces, and general war fatigue were nonetheless cited as pressures that could make a Trump-brokered opening attractive.[{N}]

Kyiv mayor [[vitali-klitschko|Vitali Klitschko]] said Zelensky risked "political suicide" if he pursued a peace deal ceding territory to Russia, telling Corriere della Sera: "How can we explain to the country that we need to give up pieces of our territory that cost the lives of thousands of our fighting heroes? Whatever move he makes, our president risks political suicide."[{N}] Klitschko predicted the coming months would be "very difficult" and suggested a referendum on any deal with Moscow would be a likely eventual scenario.[{N}]

Badlands writer [[burning-bright|Burning Bright]] described Zelensky's shift from warmonger to prospective peacemaker as "in full swing," citing the Trump call, envoys sent to China to discuss parameters of a coming peace deal, and reduced overtures to NATO for weapons deliveries, and argued that nationalist militias and globalist warmongers were now aligned against Zelensky himself.[{N}] Separate commentary by [[ghostofbasedpatrickhenry|GhostofBasedPatrickHenry]] drew a parallel with [[benjamin-netanyahu|Benjamin Netanyahu]], suggesting Zelensky faced a potential mutiny among radicalised troops should he bend the knee to Putin.[{N}]
entities/vitali-klitschko.md:
## Warning to Zelensky over territorial concessions (July 2024)

In an interview with the Italian daily Corriere della Sera published on a Sunday in July 2024, Klitschko — mayor of Kyiv and a former world heavyweight boxing champion — warned that President [[volodymyr-zelensky|Volodymyr Zelensky]] risked "political suicide" if he pursued a peace deal that ceded Ukrainian territory to Russia.[{N}] He asked: "How can we explain to the country that we need to give up pieces of our territory that cost the lives of thousands of our fighting heroes? Whatever move he makes, our president risks political suicide."[{N}] He acknowledged that the coming months would be "very difficult" for Zelensky and said the Ukrainian population would want a say in the country's fate, making a referendum on any deal with Moscow a likely future scenario.[{N}]

The statement came after a phone call between Zelensky and [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]] in which Trump signalled that peace with Russia would be a priority of his presidency.[{N}] Badlands writer [[burning-bright|Burning Bright]] characterised Klitschko's remarks as a public warning bordering on a threat, and noted Klitschko's own association with the [[azov-battalion|Azov battalion]], including his naming of a new Kyiv bridge "Azov Wave" after the unit in 2024.[{N}]
entities/azov-battalion.md:
## 3rd Assault Brigade European tour (July 2024)

Ukraine's [[3rd-assault-brigade|3rd Assault Brigade]], closely linked to the neo-Nazi Azov movement, was forced to curb a European public-relations tour in July 2024 after public backlash.[{N}] The brigade had planned events in nine cities across Poland, Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium, the Czech Republic and Lithuania between 21 July and 2 August, intending to tell attendees "only the truth about service in the brigade" and drum up support for Ukraine.[{N}] A gathering went ahead in Warsaw, but the Rotterdam welfare organisation Wmo Radar withdrew as host of "the controversial event" citing "negative media attention," and in Berlin left-wing groups planned protests, with politician Ferat Kocak saying the city "does not need additional meeting points for the extreme right."[{N}]

Kyiv mayor [[vitali-klitschko|Vitali Klitschko]] is himself associated with the Azov movement and named a new bridge in Kyiv "Azov Wave" after the battalion in 2024, according to Badlands commentary that linked Azov-aligned hardliners to domestic pressure on [[volodymyr-zelensky|Volodymyr Zelensky]] against a negotiated peace.[{N}]

## Steven van de Velde controversy (2024)

On the eve of the opening of the [[2024-paris-summer-olympics|2024 Paris Summer Olympics]], the IOC faced calls for an investigation into how a convicted child rapist had been allowed to compete.[{N}] Dutch beach volleyball player [[steven-van-de-velde|Steven van de Velde]], convicted in 2016 of raping a British 12-year-old girl, was selected for the Netherlands team, prompting warnings from advocacy groups that sporting bodies were sending a dangerous message to rapists and causing "collateral damage" to victims of sexual abuse.[{N}] Ciara Bergman, chief executive of [[rape-crisis-england-and-wales|Rape Crisis England & Wales]], called the inclusion "irresponsible," said it created an "enormous sense of impunity," and urged the IOC to investigate how it had been allowed to happen.[{N}] The IOC gave no indication it would investigate or act, on the basis that Dutch experts "had concluded that there was no risk of him reoffending."[{N}]
concepts/2024-paris-summer-olympics.md:
## Steven van de Velde scandal

The Games opened amid a scandal over the participation of Dutch beach volleyball player [[steven-van-de-velde|Steven van de Velde]], who was convicted in 2016 of raping a British 12-year-old girl and was nonetheless selected for the Netherlands team.[{N}] He had been sentenced to four years in a British prison, served about one year, was transferred to the Netherlands and released after roughly a month.[{N}] The [[international-olympic-committee|International Olympic Committee]] faced calls for an investigation from child-protection and sexual-violence advocacy groups, including [[rape-crisis-england-and-wales|Rape Crisis England & Wales]], whose chief executive Ciara Bergman said the decision created an "enormous sense of impunity."[{N}] The IOC appeared unlikely to act, on the reported basis that Dutch experts had concluded there was no risk of reoffending.[{N}]

## Clash with Elon Musk over Netanyahu address (July 2024)

On Wednesday 24 July 2024, Ocasio-Cortez and [[elon-musk|Elon Musk]] clashed on social media over Israeli prime minister [[benjamin-netanyahu|Benjamin Netanyahu]]'s address to a joint session of Congress, which she and several other Democrats boycotted.[{N}] She wrote on X: "Just so we're clear, Netanyahu has lost so many people that he is addressing just a fraction of Congress… they fill the seats with non-members, like what they do at award ceremonies, in order to project the appearance of full attendance and support."[{N}] Musk, who attended the address at the Capitol, replied that "the Democratic Party has become openly & boldly antisemitic."[{N}] Ocasio-Cortez answered, "Hmm, sometimes being quiet is free and good for you," attaching a screenshot of a Wall Street Journal article about Musk's apparent agreement with an antisemitic post in November 2023.[{N}]

Badlands commentator [[ghostofbasedpatrickhenry|GhostofBasedPatrickHenry]] said that, as someone who had defected from the "R vs D" false paradigm, he agreed with her completely and joked that she had lately been fulfilling her role as a "Judas-Goat" well, adding that dialogue is always preferable to violence.[{N}]
entities/elon-musk.md:
## Exchange with Ocasio-Cortez over Netanyahu address (July 2024)

Musk attended [[benjamin-netanyahu|Benjamin Netanyahu]]'s July 2024 address to a joint session of Congress and clashed on X with Rep. [[alexandria-ocasio-cortez|Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez]], who had boycotted the speech along with several other Democrats.[{N}] Responding to her post claiming that empty seats had been filled with non-members to project the appearance of full attendance, Musk wrote that "the Democratic Party has become openly & boldly antisemitic."[{N}] Ocasio-Cortez replied, "Hmm, sometimes being quiet is free and good for you," attaching a Wall Street Journal article about Musk's engagement in November 2023 with an antisemitic post — a conspiracy claim that Jewish people were promoting minority immigration into Western countries — for which he had come under significant criticism.[{N}]

Badlands commentary used the exchange to argue against weaponising accusations of antisemitism in political debate, citing Mossad whistleblower Victor Ostrovsky's C-SPAN account of how the term is deployed against uncooperative members of Congress, and insisting that criticism of a foreign government or its leader must remain permissible.[{N}]

## Endorsement of Kamala Harris (July 2024)

In late July 2024, NBC News reported that Obama was on the verge of publicly endorsing [[kamala-harris|Kamala Harris]] as the presumptive Democratic nominee for president, after the two spoke several times by phone in the preceding days.[{N}] The former president had privately expressed support for her candidacy and planned to endorse her soon, with discussions under way about the pair appearing together on the campaign trail; a source said he "has been in regular contact with her and thinks she's been off to a great start."[{N}]

His backing was expected to add star power to a campaign already gathering momentum: Harris travelled to Houston to give the keynote speech at the [[american-federation-of-teachers|American Federation of Teachers]] national convention, whose 1.7 million-member delegation had voted to endorse her bid, one of a flurry of endorsements from major labor unions with fewer than 100 days remaining before the presidential election.[{N}]
entities/gavin-newsom.md:
## Executive order on homeless encampments (July 2024)

On Thursday 25 July 2024, California governor Gavin Newsom ordered state agencies to begin removing homeless encampments on state land, his boldest action on the issue to that point and a response to a Supreme Court ruling allowing cities to enforce bans on sleeping outside in public spaces.[{N}] The executive order directed state agencies "to move urgently to address dangerous encampments while supporting and assisting the individuals living in them," and provided guidance to cities and counties that applied pressure without legally binding them.[{N}]

California is home to roughly one-third of the nation's homeless population, a problem that had dogged Newsom since he took office, with thousands of tents and makeshift shelters lining freeways and filling parking lots and public parks.[{N}] Under the order, agencies including state parks and the department of transportation were required to prioritise clearing encampments posing safety risks, such as those along waterways, while giving "reasonable" advance notice, offering connections to local services, and storing belongings for at least 60 days; local governments were urged to adopt similar protocols.[{N}]

## Testimony on the Butler shooting (July 2024)

On Wednesday 24 July 2024, FBI Director Christopher Wray said it was not clear whether former president [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]] had been struck by a bullet or by shrapnel when a gunman opened fire at his rally in Butler, Pennsylvania, earlier that month.[{N}] The FBI was investigating the 13 July shooting, which killed one rally-goer and seriously injured two others before the 20-year-old gunman, [[thomas-matthew-crooks|Thomas Matthew Crooks]], was shot dead by the Secret Service.[{N}]

Trump, who was rushed offstage with a bloodied ear, had said that night that he was "shot with a bullet that pierced the upper part of my right ear," describing "a whizzing sound, shots, and immediately felt the bullet ripping through the skin" in a post on Truth Social.[{N}] A week after the shooting his campaign released a doctor's note from Texas Rep. Ronny Jackson, a former White House physician, stating that Trump had sustained a gunshot wound to his right ear that came "less than a quarter of an inch from entering his head," and that he was "doing well… recovering as expected."[{N}]
